value.title: rs boot announce — seats know who they are again
value.summary: Restore the first-boot announce (announceText) for omp/pi seats under the rs daemon: the daemon reports whether a registration created, re-bound, or merely refreshed a seat row, and the extension derives 'fresh' from that instead of from 'a row exists' (which under rs is always true).

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Since c048ebc2 (2026-08-30, rs cutover) every omp/pi seat boots pij-blind: PijSession.boot injects announceText only when `fresh = registry.read(id)===null || dissolved`, and RustRuntimeSession.boot seeds every rs seat row (never reaped) into that registry BEFORE calling session.boot — so the chosen id always pre-exists (spawn pre-mints it; hand-started seats reuse by pane/process/PIJ_SESSION_ID). Last announce on disk: 2026-08-28. Live proof + mechanism: assets/inputs/diagnosis-2026-09-05.md. Fix: the daemon is the only party that knows whether /v1/register CREATED a row, RE-BOUND an existing id to a new process, or refreshed the same process; it returns that as an additive `binding` field, the TS client passes it through, and PijSession.boot accepts an explicit `fresh` override. Legacy path untouched.

sections.name: goals
value: A spawned omp seat (pij-rs spawn --harness omp --bin omp) receives announceText as its first injected turn.
A hand-started omp seat that reuses its id (same pane / same PIJ_SESSION_ID) still announces on the first session_start of a NEW process.
/new, /fork, reload on a live seat do not announce twice (the original 'exactly one inject at boot' rule survives).
The rs register contract carries the fact additively (`binding: created|rebound|same`), shared by both runtimes through one golden fixture.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Reaping or tombstoning stale rs seat rows (separate roadmap question, plan 095 evidence pointer).
Changing announceText content or the ready-ping protocol (PIJ_ANNOUNCE_TO path).
Any legacy-daemon behaviour; the legacy TS daemon is stopped for good.

value.claim: spawned omp seat announces on first boot
value.text: LIVE on the rs daemon: `pij-rs spawn --harness omp --bin omp` → the seat's first injected user turn is announceText (`You are pij session <id> …`), captured from the omp session jsonl AND the pane; the spine shows seat.put then the announce inject. CONTROL first on main 46c9314c: same gesture, no announce (paste both).

value.claim: hand-started seat with a reused id announces on a new process
value.text: Start omp by hand in a tmux pane whose id already carries an rs seat row (or with PIJ_SESSION_ID set to an existing idle seat): register returns binding=rebound (proc changed) and the announce fires once. Paste register response + session jsonl.

value.claim: no double announce on /new, /fork or reload
value.text: On a live seat run /new then /reload: register returns binding=same for the reload and exactly one announce exists per NEW pi session id; rust-runtime.test.ts asserts inject(announceText) count per reason.

value.claim: register contract is additive and shared
value.text: `/v1/register` response gains `binding` (created|rebound|same) with no renamed or removed field; one golden fixture docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/register-response.json is deserialized by a Rust test (crates/daemon) AND parsed by a TS test (core/daemon-wire) — both cite the same file path in their source.

value.claim: the witness was red before it was green
value.text: The new rs-path announce test is run against the pre-fix tree first and its failing output is pasted (witness-never-failed rule); then green on the fix.

value.claim: legacy path and full gates untouched
value.text: core/session.test.ts unchanged and green; `harness checks` green; `cargo test --workspace`, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check green on the composed branch; outputs pasted.

value.title: Contract, then units, then live proof
value.name: u0 contract → u1 rust ∥ u2 ts → compose + live
value.brief: Freeze the binding vocabulary and golden fixture (u0, PM), fan out u1 (Rust: store insert/rebind detection + register response) and u2 (TS: pass-through + fresh override + RED-first test), compose, then the live spawn proof.
